preview: Goldman Sachs internship interview experience featuring an aptitude test, coding rounds, technical interviews covering DSA and system design, and preparation advice.
content: Goldman Sachs Interview Experience (Internship) Saif Kazi | T.Y. B.Tech CE 2018-22 Aptitude Test (100+ participants) 27th August, 2020 The test was conducted on Hackerrank. It included multiple sections. Each section had a corresponding timer. You cannot submit answers to any questions of that section if its timer runs out. You can attempt the sections themselves in any order. Section 1 (30 mins) 1. I don’t remember the question exactly but the first one was based on array traversal. I was able to pass 11/12 test cases. For the last case, answer modulo 109+7 was required though it wasn’t mentioned in the question. 2. We have coordinates of the starting and destination points in a 2D plane. We also have a list of pairs of points where each pair represents a straight line that passes through that pair of points. The task was to find the minimum euclidean distance of the path from start to destination point without crossing over any of the lines. However, you can pass through the endpoints of the line. For example, starting point is (0,0) destination point is (3,0) and there is a line passing through (1,0) and (2,1) so the shortest path would (0,0) -> (1,0) -> (3,0) with distance 3. I was able to pass 6 out of the 12 test cases. Section 2 (~20 mins) 10 math MCQs. +5, -2 marking scheme. Questions were based on probability, trigonometry, geometry, and number theory. Will remind you of your JEE days. I didn’t attempt a single question from this section. Section 3 (~15 mins) 7 CS subjects’ based MCQs. +5, -2 marking scheme Questions were from OS, DBMS, Computer Networking, Computer Architecture. There was a question about LRU page replacement policy. A question for which we were given a code and we had to select the bottom-up dynamic programming code for that function. I was able to solve 5 out of 7 questions. Section 4 (~40 mins) 1. We were given an MxN matrix consisting of numbers from 1 to F where each number represents a different type of flower. We had to print the number of cells in the largest connected component of the graph with at most 2 different types of flowers in it. You can move in any of the 4 perpendicular directions from a cell. You can start from any cell as well. I was able to solve only the 2 sample cases provided. Section 5 (~15 mins) 1. Write about an experience that shows your passion. 2. How will you handle a situation wherein you’re facing a deadline and your team member won’t be to work due to some emergency? Honestly, nobody cares if you answer these or not. 29 candidates were shortlisted for the interview rounds. (All interview rounds were conducted on the same day) Interview Round 1 - (Technical) (~25 mins) 2nd September, 2020 The questions of this round varied from interviewer to interviewer. Some candidates were asked about their projects, or system design or CS subjects. The coding was done over Hackerrank Codepair. The interview rounds took place on Zoom. The interviewer started by asking me to introduce myself. Use this opportunity to direct the interview in the direction you want. Then she asked me 3 DSA questions - 1. https://java2blog.com/given-sorted-array-number-x-find-pair-closest-to-x-array/ I gave an O(N2) solution and then an O(NlogN) binary search based approach. She asked me if I knew how to implement binary search. I wasn’t asked to code the solution. 2. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/pairwise-swap-adjacent-nodes-of-a-linked-list-by-changing-pointers-set-2/ I was asked to code the while loop for this question. 3. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/maximum-possible-time-that-can-be-formed-from-four-digits/ Make sure you cover all the conditions for this question. Once again I wasn’t asked to code the solution. The interviewer asked if I had any questions. Always ask a question, you can learn a lot from the interviewer’s experience. 16 candidates were shortlisted for Round 2. Interview Round 2 (Technical) (~50 mins) The interviewer started by asking me to introduce myself. Since I mentioned projects in my introduction, he asked me to talk about any one of my projects and a few questions on it followed. Then he asked me Q.1 of Round 1. 1. This time the array is not sorted. Find 2 numbers whose sum is k. I gave an O(N2), O(NlogN), O(N) hash table based solution. 2. For the same question find 3 numbers whose sum is k. I was heading in the wrong direction and the interviewer gave some hints. In the end, I came with an O(N2) solution and he seemed satisfied. 3. He updated Q.1 and asked me to write a function that gives all such pairs. I told him my approach to store all pairs found and then he changed the question. 4. Now the array contains duplicate elements. Find all pairs in this case. I made the mistake of assuming (5,10) and (10,5) are the same. Never assume anything and always clarify things with the interviewer. Finally the question was given the array {0,5,6,5,9,10,10} and k=15, output should be (5,10),(5,10),(5,10),(5,10),(6,9) I managed an O(N2) time and O(N) space solution and he seemed satisfied. Then the interviewer asked if I had any questions. Always ask a question. Asking a good question shows that you are interested. (Which you should be since you applied xD) 7 candidates were shortlisted for Round 3. Interview Round 3 (Technical + HR) (~50 mins) There were 2 interviewers in this round. Once again they started with “Introduce yourself”. Since I mentioned hackathons, they asked a few questions on it. Then they asked a few DSA questions, 1. Explain binary search and state its prerequisite. 2. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/search-an-element-in-a-sorted-and-pivoted-array/ 3. Find the depth of a binary tree. 4. Now the leaf nodes of the binary tree have been modified so that their left and right pointers now point to the corresponding left and right leaves to that leaf. Find the depth of this tree. I was asked to code a function for this. 5. The interviewer picked a question on Hackerrank and said he himself didn’t know the solution so he suggested we solve it together. We came up with a brute force solution. Apparently the question was a standard range update question and required segment trees. I wasn’t aware of it. He said that’s okay. He asked me to code the brute force solution. 6. Next, they asked me what deadlock is and the conditions for deadlock. 7. Then they asked me how I would scale a website so that it can handle 50,000 requests. 8. You are part of a team that has to deliver a product to the client. You need infrastructure but let’s say the cloud team isn’t providing you that because you are not a priority for them. How do you deal with this situation? 9. Are you willing to relocate? They asked if I had any questions. Always ask a question. In the end, 6 candidates were shortlisted and were asked to pitch themselves and the best candidate would be selected. But that was a prank and all 6 candidates were offered internships. Preparation 1. Pick one platform and stick to it. No need to cycle through all coding platforms. 2. GeeksforGeeks has a good amount of articles on all topics and data structures and you can filter questions based on companies as well. 3. To practice coding under a time limit try Interviewbit. 4. Read interview experiences for all the companies. That will give you a good feel of how interviews are conducted. The exact format may change but you’ll notice a pattern in them. 5. Start preparing for CS subjects early. Don’t leave them for the last week. No matter how much you cram, you won’t be able to cover everything. Advice 1. Practice introducing yourself. You may think you know what you are going to say. But sometimes it doesn’t come out the same. So practice. 2. Use your introduction to direct the interview in the direction you want. For me, I wanted them to focus on my projects, so mentioned that I like to work on projects in my introduction and all my interview rounds started with them talking about my projects. 3. The interviewer is not your enemy. If you get stuck, pay attention to what the interviewer says. They may give you a test case where your code would fail or even directly suggest you alternate approaches. 4. Research the company you are going to interview for. It helps if you know what the company does. 5. Always ask questions at the end of the interview. You get to learn a lot through that and you can use that information to strike a conversation with the next interviewer. 6. If you are into development more so than competitive coding, don’t feel discouraged. Direct the interview in that direction and everything will be fine. 7. Be ready well before your interview’s starting time. 8. Be patient. There can be delays in either taking the interviews or announcing the results. 9. It’s okay to be nervous as long as you don’t let it come in the middle of your thinking. Stay Calm and Best of Luck!!
